key_insight: The paper identifies and closes a gap in evaluation by providing a reliable, visual-centric framework to measure how faithfully multimodal LLMs follow instructions that depend on images — revealing failures missed by text-only benchmarks.
problem_solved: Existing instruction-following benchmarks emphasize textual prompts and ignore implicit visual constraints, preventing accurate assessment and improvement of MLLMs' ability to follow image-grounded user intentions.
method: Design a visual-centric benchmark of image + instruction tasks that include explicit and implicit visual constraints (e.g., spatial relations, occlusion-aware actions).
Define evaluation metrics and a protocol that quantify fidelity to user intent, constraint satisfaction, and failure modes (precision, constraint-violation rates, targeted error categories).
Evaluate representative MLLMs with controlled prompts to expose common instruction-following gaps and provide baselines for future improvements.
impact: Provides practitioners a focused toolset to diagnose, compare, and improve multimodal models on real-world image-grounded instruction tasks, accelerating development of more reliable and aligned MLLMs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image + visual instruction → model → expected vs. actual output (highlight constraint violations).
Bar chart: comparison of models on fidelity/constraint-satisfaction metrics with error-rate stacked segments.
Example panel: 3 side-by-side image tasks showing correct behavior, common failure, and proposed metric assessment.
Rubric iconography: small infographic showing key evaluation criteria (fidelity, completeness, safety).
paper_title: Empowering Reliable Visual-Centric Instruction Following in MLLMs
paper_authors: Weilei He, Feng Ju, Zhiyuan Fan, Rui Min, Minhao Cheng
